summary.title: Microsoft Azure in Plain English
summary.one_liner: A satirical, service-by-service guide to Microsoft Azure's products, each mapped to rough AWS and other-vendor equivalents.
keywords: azure cloud services vs virtual machines
cloud service mapping aws ec2 s3 lambda
takeaways: Azure services are grouped by domain: web/apps, storage, management, mobile, media/CDN, networking, enterprise, big data and IoT.
Each Azure product is given a plain-language purpose and a comparable AWS or third-party service (e.g., Blob Storage ~ AWS S3, Virtual Network ~ AWS VPC).
App Service, Cloud Services and Virtual Machines differ mainly in how much server administration you take on (PaaS, IaaS-style, raw VMs).
The page is a humorous, opinionated take rather than official documentation, so verify details against Microsoft's current docs.
summary.summary: This is a satirical 'Plain English' explainer from 2019 (archived on the Wayback Machine) that walks through Microsoft Azure's product catalog. Services are grouped into categories such as Web and Apps, Storage, Management, Mobile, Media and CDN, Networking, Enterprise, Big Data and IoT. For each one it gives a short 'use this to...' description, a joke 'should have been called' name, and a comparable AWS or third-party product. It is a quick mapping reference for someone already familiar with AWS, not a technical tutorial, and it does not include prices or configuration steps.
